instructions: Glance is the user's document and image viewer on Windows. Use it to look at and work with local files: see any page or image (PDF, camera RAW, HEIC, PSD, JPEG XL, EPS, XPS, TIFF, comics and 40+ other formats), read text with OCR, combine, split, rotate and reorder PDF pages, convert images, and redact text so it is really removed. Paths are absolute Windows paths and pages are numbered from 1. Tools never change the files you pass in: every edit writes a new file at output_path. The glance_open, glance_list_open, glance_current_view, glance_go_to_page, glance_mark_redactions, glance_text_layout, glance_edit_text, glance_add_text and glance_erase tools work with what the user has open in the Glance window; the editing ones change the open document in its own style, for the user to review and save. Glance also creates and edits slide decks (glance_create, glance_deck_edit): send the content and pick layouts, and Glance does the design. For a polished deck, prefer a template's designed slides (glance_templates lists them) and keep each slot's text within its maxChars. It makes documents too (.gdoc files: letters, reports, CVs, newsletters, invoices, certificates): glance_create with kind document and a template, then glance_doc_outline, glance_doc_edit, glance_doc_check and glance_doc_render; send words and blocks, and the template's look does the design. Glance makes spreadsheets too (.xlsx and .csv, with live formulas): glance_create with kind spreadsheet (optionally from a template), then glance_sheet_read, glance_sheet_edit, glance_sheet_check and glance_sheet_render. Before making or changing a deck, document or spreadsheet, read the matching Glance skill (resources skill://glance/slide-design/SKILL.md, skill://glance/document-writing/SKILL.md, skill://glance/spreadsheet-building/SKILL.md, and skill://glance/editing/SKILL.md for changes) or use the create-deck, create-document, create-spreadsheet and edit-file prompts: they hold Glance's design and writing rules. Write a placeholder like [date] for any fact you don't have instead of inventing it. Use these tools whenever the user asks about a local document or image, or about what they're looking at, even if they don't mention Glance. Glance starts in the background by itself when a tool needs it, so never ask the user to open it first.

tools.name: glance_info
tools.title: File info
tools.description: Describes a document, image or 3D model: its kind, size, page count, image dimensions, PDF metadata (title, author, page sizes, whether pages have selectable text) and photo metadata (camera, date, location). Use it before working with an unfamiliar file.

tools.name: glance_view
tools.title: View a page or image
tools.description: Renders one page of a PDF, PostScript/EPS, XPS, multi-page TIFF or comic book, or an image in any format Glance opens (camera RAW, HEIC/AVIF, PSD, JPEG XL, JPEG 2000, EXR/HDR, DDS, ICNS, SVG, …) and returns it as an image you can look at.

page.description: Page or frame to show, from 1. Default 1.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels. Default 1568.

tools.name: glance_read_text
tools.title: Read text
tools.description: Returns the text of a PDF (per page) or of an image. Pages without selectable text (scans, photos of documents) and images are read with Windows OCR.

pages.description: Pages to read, like "1-3,7" or "5-". Default: all.

ocr.description: auto (default): OCR only pages without selectable text. always: OCR every page, for garbled text layers. never: selectable text only.

tools.name: glance_convert
tools.title: Convert
tools.description: Saves a page or image as a new file. The format follows output_path's extension: .png, .jpg, .webp, .tif, .bmp or .pdf. Works with every format Glance opens, so it can turn RAW, HEIC, PSD or a PDF page into a JPEG or PNG, or an image into a PDF.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to convert.

output_path.description: Absolute path of the new file. Must not exist yet unless overwrite is true.

page.description: Page or frame to convert, from 1. Default 1.

max_size.description: Scale down so the longest side is at most this many pixels. PDF pages render at 200 dpi by default.

overwrite.description: Replace output_path if it exists. Default false.

tools.name: glance_combine
tools.title: Combine into PDF
tools.description: Combines PDFs and images, in the order given, into one new PDF. Each image becomes a page.

inputs.description: Absolute paths of the PDFs and images, in order.

output_path.description: Absolute path of the new PDF. Must not exist yet unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace output_path if it exists. Default false.

tools.name: glance_pdf_pages
tools.title: Edit PDF pages
tools.description: Makes a new PDF from an existing one with pages extracted, deleted, rotated or reordered, or splits it into several PDFs. extract keeps only `pages`; delete removes `pages`; rotate turns `pages` (default all) by `degrees`; reorder uses `order`, a full list of page numbers in their new order; split writes one PDF per `every` pages, or starts a new PDF at each of `pages`, named after output_path with " 1", " 2", … added.

output_path.description: Absolute path of the new PDF (for split, the name the parts are numbered after). Must not exist yet unless overwrite is true.

pages.description: Pages like "1-3,7" or "5-". For split: the first page of each part after the first.

order.description: reorder: every page number exactly once, in the new order.

overwrite.description: Replace existing output files. Default false.

tools.name: glance_redact
tools.title: Redact text
tools.description: Finds text in a PDF or image and saves a redacted copy where it is truly gone: affected PDF pages are flattened to images with the text painted out and hidden copies (text layer, annotations, form fields, metadata) removed. Scanned pages and images are searched with OCR. Set dry_run to only list what would be redacted.

path.description: Absolute path of the PDF or image.

output_path.description: Absolute path of the redacted copy. Must not exist yet unless overwrite is true. Not needed for dry_run.

patterns.description: Kinds of personal data to redact: email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, ID numbers (SSN, national ID), bank accounts (IBAN), dates.

regex.description: A JavaScript regular expression to redact matches of.

pages.description: Only these pages, like "1-3,7". Default: all.

dry_run.description: Only report the matches; write nothing. Default false.

overwrite.description: Replace output_path if it exists. Default false.

tools.name: glance_remove_location
tools.title: Remove location
tools.description: Saves a copy of a photo without its GPS location (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, HEIC, JPEG XL). Everything else, pixels included, stays as it was.

output_path.description: Absolute path of the copy, same extension. Must not exist yet unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace output_path if it exists. Default false.

tools.name: glance_open
tools.title: Open in Glance
tools.description: Opens files in the Glance window for the user to see (each in its own tab), brings the window to the front, and optionally goes to a page of the first file.

page.description: Page to show in the first file.

tools.name: glance_list_open
tools.title: List open tabs
tools.description: Lists the documents open in the Glance window: tab id, name, path, kind, the page the user is on, page count, selected pages, unsaved changes, and which tab is active.

tools.name: glance_current_view
tools.title: What the user sees
tools.description: Returns the page the user is looking at in Glance (the active tab, or `tab`) as an image, with its text, including unsaved markup and edits.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels. Default 1568.

tools.name: glance_go_to_page
tools.title: Go to page
tools.description: Shows a page in an open document in Glance.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_mark_redactions
tools.title: Mark for redaction
tools.description: Marks text in a PDF open in Glance for redaction, for the user to review and apply (nothing is removed until they choose Apply Redactions). Takes the same search options as glance_redact.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_text_layout
tools.title: Page text and style
tools.description: Lists the paragraphs on a page of the PDF or image open in Glance, with an id for each, its text, where it is, and its look: font, size, bold, italic, colour and line spacing. Images are read with Windows OCR. Call it before glance_edit_text or glance_add_text to see the exact wording and style. Edits the AI already made are included.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Default: the page the user is on.

tools.name: glance_edit_text
tools.title: Edit text
tools.description: Changes text in the PDF or image open in Glance, in the same font, size, colour and line spacing as the text around it. The words after the change move along, and the paragraph is laid out again when it gets longer or shorter. An empty replace deletes the text. Give find (exact text within one paragraph, as glance_text_layout shows it) or paragraph (an id, to replace the whole paragraph). Without page, the page the user is on is searched first, then the others. The change is drawn over the original as markup the user can review and undo; nothing is saved to disk until they save. For several separate changes, call it once per change.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Default: the page the user is on.

find.description: Exact text to change, within one paragraph.

paragraph.description: Paragraph id from glance_text_layout, to replace the whole paragraph.

occurrence.description: Which match to change, from 1, or "all". Default 1.

make_room.description: Move the text below down when the new text needs more room. Default true.

font.description: Font family to use instead of the page's (an installed Windows font).

size.description: Font size in points, instead of the page's.

color.description: Text colour as #rrggbb, instead of the page's.

tools.name: glance_add_text
tools.title: Add text
tools.description: Writes new text into the PDF or image open in Glance in the page's own style: after or before a paragraph (same left edge, width, font, size, colour and spacing), or at a point. like copies the look of another paragraph (for example a heading). Lines wrap like the page's. The text is markup the user can review, move and undo.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Default: the page the user is on.

text.description: The text to add. New lines start new lines.

after.description: Paragraph id, or text in the paragraph, to put it after.

before.description: Paragraph id, or text in the paragraph, to put it before.

at.description: Where its top-left corner goes, as fractions of the page from the top-left (0 to 1), and how wide it is.

like.description: Paragraph id, or text in it, whose look to copy.

make_room.description: Move the text below down when the new text needs more room. Default true.

font.description: Font family to use instead of the page's (an installed Windows font).

size.description: Font size in points, instead of the page's.

color.description: Text colour as #rrggbb, instead of the page's.

tools.name: glance_erase
tools.title: Erase
tools.description: Removes a paragraph or an area from the PDF or image open in Glance by covering it with its background: the surrounding colour on plain backgrounds, or a fill blended from the surrounding pixels on photos and textured backgrounds. The user can review and undo it. To remove sensitive text for good, use glance_mark_redactions instead.

tab.description: Tab id or path from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Default: the page the user is on.

paragraph.description: Paragraph id, or text in it.

area.description: Fractions of the page from the top-left (0 to 1).

tools.name: glance_plan
tools.title: Show a plan
tools.description: Shows your plan for a new deck, document or spreadsheet on Glance's Outline screen, where the user can reorder, rename, delete and add items, answer your questions, pick a look and choose how many words, then build it. Use it when Glance asks you to plan first (the Ask AI sidebar does for new files), then stop and wait: the user's next message says to build it, with their changes, or what to change. Each item is one slide, section or page, or sheet, with a short title and a line on what goes there; for a template, also the design id it uses. Ask at most three short questions, only for facts only the user knows (a date, a place, a price); anything left unanswered becomes a placeholder like [date].

tab.description: Tab id of the new file, from Glance's message or glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

audience.description: Who it is for and the one thing they should take away, in a line.

items.description: The slides, sections or sheets in order: {title, detail?, design?}. detail says what goes there in a line; design is a template design id like "bakeSale.2".

look.description: The look you suggest: a template id from glance_templates, or for a deck without a template a theme (wollo, wolloDark, sunrise, blossom, ink).

questions.description: Up to three short questions for facts only the user knows.

tools.name: glance_templates
tools.title: List templates
tools.description: Lists Glance's designed templates of every kind: decks (kind deck) and documents (kind document). A document template is a look: its designs are pages, fixed (a poster, invoice or certificate: text boxes with name, hint and maxChars, and tables, some worked out) or flowing (an essay, letter or report page whose blocks flow across as many pages as needed), plus a plain page (<id>.plain), its styles (body, h1 to h3, quote, caption and the template's own, with what each is for) and colours. Pack templates are sets of one-page documents. For decks: Each template has an id, name, purpose (School, Work, Events, Personal or Clubs) and look, and its designs: designed slides with an id (like "bakeSale.2"), what the slide is for (cover, stats, timeline, map, thank you and so on) and its text slots, each with a name, a hint (the template's own sample text, which shows what goes there and how long it is) and maxChars, the most characters that fit at the design's size. Prefer these designs for a polished deck, fill every slot, and keep each within its maxChars. The result also lists spreadsheets: Glance's spreadsheet templates, each with an id, name, blurb, purpose and sheets, for glance_create with kind spreadsheet.

template.description: One template's id, to list only its designs. Default: every template.

kind.description: Only templates of this kind. Default: every kind.

tools.name: glance_create
tools.title: Create a deck, document or spreadsheet
tools.description: Creates a slide deck (kind deck), a document (kind document) or a spreadsheet (kind spreadsheet) in Glance from your content and opens it for the user. A document: pass template (a document template id from glance_templates; default essay) and either nothing (the template as it is, with its sample text; for a pack, pass design to pick its page), pages (a list of {design, texts?, tables?, blocks?}: design is one of the template's design ids or its number, or plain; texts fill a fixed page's text boxes by name within maxChars; tables give rows of text cells without the header; blocks fill a flowing page), or blocks alone (one flowing section in the template's flowing page). Blocks: {type:'heading', level 1-3, text}, {type:'paragraph', text, style?}, {type:'list', items, ordered?}, {type:'quote', text, cite?}, {type:'callout', blocks}, {type:'table', rows, header?, footer?}, {type:'picture', src, alt, caption?, width?}, {type:'chart', chart: bar|line|pie, rows (a header row, then label and numbers), title?, caption?}, {type:'divider'}, {type:'columns', columns: [[blocks], [blocks]]}, {type:'pageBreak'}. Text takes **bold**, *italic* and [links](https://...); style names one of the look's styles. Pass from (a .docx path) to convert a Word file into a document instead; the result says what was left out. Output paths end in .gdoc. For a deck: You choose each slide's layout and fill its slots with words and pictures; Glance's layouts and theme handle position, fonts, colours and fitting, so never describe looks in the text. Good decks: one idea per slide, a title slide first, short phrases rather than sentences, and a mix of layouts (threeCards, bigNumber, timeline, quote, imageRight) instead of bullets on every slide; put detail in notes (what the speaker says). The result lists the slide ids and the design check's findings: fix those with glance_deck_edit, then look at the slides with glance_deck_render. For a polished, designed deck, start from a template instead (glance_templates lists them): pass template and slides of {design, slots, notes?}, where design is one of that template's design ids (like "bakeSale.3", or just its number, 3) and slots fills every slot that design lists, each within its maxChars. Use any of the template's designs in any order and as often as you need, so a 12-slide deck can repeat designs; a deck's designs all come from one template. Leave slides out to start from the template's own slides and sample text, then change them with glance_deck_edit. A designed slide has layout design. Layouts and their slots (* = required; numbers are the most characters, or entries, that fit): title: title* (60), subtitle (120), image (picture). section: title* (50), subtitle (100). bullets: title* (60), bullets* (list of text, up to 6, 70 each). twoColumns: title* (60), left* and right* (lists of text, up to 5, 60 each). imageLeft and imageRight: title* (60), image* (picture), body (280). fullImage: image* (picture), caption (90). bigNumber: stat* (8, like "92%" or "£1,240"), statLabel* (60), body (160). threeCards: title* (60), items* (3 of {heading, body}, 80 together). quote: quote* (220), attribution (60). comparison: title* (60), table* (rows of text cells, the first row is the header; up to 7 rows, 40 per cell). timeline: title* (60), items* (up to 6 of {heading, body}, 60 together). A picture is {src, alt, focus?}: src is the absolute path of a local PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, AVIF or SVG (Glance copies it into the deck) or a media/ path the deck already has; alt describes it for people who can't see it; focus {x, y} (0 to 1 from the top left) keeps the subject in view when it is cropped. With kind spreadsheet, it creates a workbook instead: pass title, template (a spreadsheet template id from glance_templates; it starts with sample data and live formulas) and ops (as in glance_sheet_edit) to fill it, and output_path ending in .xlsx to save it. The result lists its sheets and the workbook check's findings.

kind.description: What to create: a slide deck, a document or a spreadsheet.

title.description: The deck's name, used for its file name. Default: the first slide's title.

theme.description: wollo (default): ink on white with violet. wolloDark: light text on near black with soft violet. sunrise: warm cream with orange, for classes and clubs. blossom: white with pink, for celebrations and stories. ink: near black with yellow, for numbers and reports. Designed slides keep their template's own look.

template.description: A template id from glance_templates, like bakeSale: the deck is made of that template's designs. Without slides, the deck starts as the template is, with its sample text. For a document or spreadsheet, a template id of that kind.

ops.description: Spreadsheet only: operations to apply once it is created, as in glance_sheet_edit.

slides.description: The slides in order: {layout, slots: {slot name: value}, notes?}, or for a designed slide {design, slots, notes?}. Slot values are text, a list of text, a list of {heading, body}, rows of text cells, or a picture, as the layout says; a design's slots all take text.

pages.description: Documents: the pages in order, each {design, texts?, tables?, blocks?}.

blocks.description: Documents: flowing blocks for one section in the template's flowing page.

design.description: Documents from a pack template: which page to start from (a design id or number). Default: its first.

from.description: Documents: absolute path of a .docx to convert into a Glance document in the template's look.

output_path.description: Absolute path ending in .gdeck (a deck), .gdoc (a document) or .xlsx (a spreadsheet) to save it at. Default: it opens unsaved, and the user picks where to save it.

overwrite.description: Replace output_path if it exists. Default false.

tools.name: glance_deck_outline
tools.title: Read a deck
tools.description: Returns a deck open in Glance as JSON: its theme and each slide's id, number, layout (and design, for a template's designed slide), slots, notes and whether it is hidden. Edits the user made are included. Use the ids with glance_deck_edit.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open deck, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_deck_edit
tools.title: Edit a deck
tools.description: Changes a deck open in Glance with a list of operations, applied in order as one step the user can undo. If any operation is invalid nothing changes, and the error says which one and why. Operations: {op:'add', layout, slots?, notes?, after?} (after: a slide id, or null for first; default last), or {op:'add', design, slots?, notes?, after?} for a template's designed slide (a design id from glance_templates; fill every slot, within its maxChars); {op:'move', ids, after} (after: an id, or null for first); {op:'delete', ids}; {op:'duplicate', id}; {op:'hide', ids, hidden}; {op:'setLayout', id, layout} or {op:'setLayout', id, design} (slots the new layout or design lacks are dropped and reported); {op:'setSlot', id, slot, value}; {op:'clearSlot', id, slot}; {op:'setNotes', id, notes}; {op:'setTheme', theme}; {op:'split', id} (moves the second half of a list onto a new slide after it); {op:'merge', ids: [a, b]} (same layout; b's list joins a's). Layouts, slot values and pictures are as in glance_create. The result has the new slide ids and the design check's findings.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open deck, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_deck_check
tools.title: Check a deck's design
tools.description: Lists what to fix in a deck open in Glance before the user sees it: missing required slots (every slot of a designed slide), text too long for its layout or design, lists with too many entries, three slides in a row with the same layout, no title slide, and pictures without alt text. Each finding names the slide id and says what to do. An empty list means the deck passes. Placeholders in square brackets like [date] are listed separately (placeholders): they are left for the user to fill, so leave them unless you know the fact.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open deck, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_deck_render
tools.title: Look at slides
tools.description: Returns slides of a deck open in Glance as images, exactly as the user sees them, so you can check your work. Up to 12 slides per call.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open deck, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

slides.description: Slide numbers like "1-3,7", or slide ids separated by commas. Default: the slide the user is on.

max_size.description: Width of each image in pixels. Default 960.

tools.name: glance_doc_outline
tools.title: Read a document
tools.description: Returns a Glance document (.gdoc) open in Glance as JSON: its look, page count, the user's current page and selection, the look's style names, and each section's id, design, what it is for, whether it is fixed or flowing and which pages it fills; a fixed page's text boxes (name, text, hint and maxChars, the most characters that fit) and tables (columns, rows, worked-out columns); a flowing page's blocks with their ids, types and text (**bold**, *italic*, [links](url)). Edits the user made are included. Use the ids with glance_doc_edit.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open document, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_doc_edit
tools.title: Edit a document
tools.description: Changes a document open in Glance with a list of operations, applied in order as one step the user can keep or undo. If any operation is invalid nothing changes, and the error says which one and why. Operations: {op:'addBlocks', blocks, section?, after?} (after a block id, or null for the start of section; default the end of the last flowing section); {op:'replaceBlock', id, block} (the block keeps its id); {op:'moveBlocks', ids, after, section?}; {op:'deleteBlocks', ids}; {op:'setText', section, box, text} (a fixed page's text box, within its maxChars; empty clears it); {op:'addSection', design, after?, texts?, tables?, blocks?} (a new page from the look's designs, or <look>.plain); {op:'deleteSection', ids}; {op:'moveSection', ids, after}; {op:'setLook', look} (another document template's look; flowing text keeps flowing, fixed pages keep the boxes the new page has, and what is dropped is reported); {op:'addRow', id or section and table, cells, at?}; {op:'deleteRow', id or section and table, row}; {op:'setCell', id or section and table, row, col, text}; {op:'setRows', id or section and table, rows}. Rows count from 0 without a fixed table's header; worked-out columns and totals are filled in by Glance. Blocks are as in glance_create; a picture's src may be an absolute path (Glance copies it in). The result has the new ids, the page count and the document check's findings.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open document, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_doc_check
tools.title: Check a document
tools.description: Lists what to fix in a document open in Glance before the user sees it: empty text boxes on fixed pages, text too long for its box, tables with more rows than the page fits, empty blocks, headings that skip a level, paragraphs too long or too many in a row, ragged tables and pictures without alt text. Each finding names the section, block or box and says what to do. An empty list means the document passes.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open document, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_doc_render
tools.title: Look at document pages
tools.description: Returns pages of a document open in Glance as images, exactly as the user sees them, so you can check your work. Up to 12 pages per call.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open document, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

pages.description: Page numbers like "1-3,7", or section ids separated by commas (every page they fill). Default: the page the user is on.

max_size.description: Width of each image in pixels. Default 800.

tools.name: glance_word_replace
tools.title: Replace text in a Word file
tools.description: Replaces every occurrence of some text in a Word file (.docx) and writes the result to a new file, leaving the original as it is. Only the text changes: formatting, layout, pictures and the rest of the file stay as Word wrote them. Text that Word split across formatting changes can't be matched; try a shorter piece. The result says how many places changed.

path.description: Absolute path of the .docx to read.

find.description: The text to replace, as it appears in the document.

replace.description: The new text. Empty deletes it.

overwrite.description: Replace output_path if it exists. Default false.

tools.name: glance_sheet_read
tools.title: Read a spreadsheet
tools.description: Returns a spreadsheet open in Glance as JSON: each sheet's name, used range, frozen panes, tables with their headers, drop-downs and rules, charts and conditional formats; the user's selection; and the cells of one sheet as [ref, value, =formula, number format]. Values are what the formulas give now, and edits the user made are included. Read before you change data, and use the headers and ranges with glance_sheet_edit.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open spreadsheet, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

sheet.description: Sheet name. Default: the active sheet.

range.description: Cells to return, like A1:H40. Default: the used range.

tools.name: glance_sheet_edit
tools.title: Edit a spreadsheet
tools.description: Changes a spreadsheet open in Glance with a list of operations, applied in order as one step the user can undo. If any operation is invalid nothing changes, and the error says which one and why. Every op but the sheet ones takes sheet (default: the active sheet). Operations: {op:'set', cell, value} or {op:'set', cell, formula:'=SUM(B2:B9)'} or {op:'set', range, values: rows of values}, each with an optional style; {op:'clear', range, what?: all|contents|formats}; {op:'fill', from, to} (copies cells and adjusts their formulas); {op:'insertRows'|'deleteRows', at: row number, count?}; {op:'insertCols'|'deleteCols', at: column letter, count?}; {op:'addSheet', name, after?, copyOf?}; {op:'deleteSheet', name}; {op:'renameSheet', sheet, to}; {op:'moveSheet', name, index}; {op:'format', range, style} (style: bold, italic, color, fill, numFmt like '£#,##0.00' or 'd mmm yyyy', align, wrap, border, fontSize); {op:'merge'|'unmerge', range}; {op:'colWidth', cols, width}; {op:'rowHeight', rows, height}; {op:'hide'|'show', cols?, rows?} (with neither, the sheet itself); {op:'addCf', range, rule} (rule types dataBar, colorScale, iconSet, cellIs, expression, text); {op:'clearCf', range}; {op:'addValidation', range, rule} (a list for a drop-down, whole, decimal or date limits, or a tick box); {op:'clearValidation', range}; {op:'addChart', chart}; {op:'updateChart', id, chart}; {op:'deleteChart', id}; {op:'sort', range, by: [{col, desc?}], header?}; {op:'filter', range?, col?, values?}; {op:'freeze', rows?, cols?}; {op:'tabColor', color}; {op:'activate', sheet}. Glance works out formulas as you edit. A chart is kept as Glance's own model in the .xlsx, with a picture of it for other apps. The result has the workbook check's findings.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open spreadsheet, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_sheet_check
tools.title: Check a spreadsheet
tools.description: Lists what to fix in a spreadsheet open in Glance: formulas that give an error, references to deleted cells, functions Glance doesn't know, and values that break a cell's drop-down or rule. Each finding names the sheet and cell. An empty list means the workbook passes.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open spreadsheet, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

tools.name: glance_sheet_render
tools.title: Look at a sheet
tools.description: Returns a picture of one sheet of a spreadsheet open in Glance, with its formatting, conditional formats and charts, so you can check your work.

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open spreadsheet, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

sheet.description: Sheet name. Default: the active sheet.

tools.name: glance_export
tools.title: Export a deck, document or spreadsheet
tools.description: Saves a deck, document or spreadsheet open in Glance. A document exports as PDF (its art as a picture and its text as real text), Word (.docx: real headings, lists and tables, the page art behind the text and text boxes as frames) or PNG pictures, one per page. A deck exports as a PDF, a PowerPoint file (.pptx, with speaker notes and hidden slides kept) or PNG pictures, one per shown slide (named "<output_path stem> 01.png" and so on). Exports look the same as the deck in Glance. PowerPoint shows the deck's fonts only where they are installed. A spreadsheet exports as xlsx, csv (the active sheet), pdf (every shown sheet, fitted to the page width) or png (the active sheet).

tab.description: Tab id or path of an open deck, document or spreadsheet, from glance_list_open. Default: the active tab.

format.description: pdf, pptx (decks), docx (documents), xlsx or csv (spreadsheets), or png.

output_path.description: Absolute path for the file, ending in .pdf, .pptx, .docx, .xlsx, .csv or .png.

overwrite.description: Replace files that exist. Default false.
